name: Choose and execute a registered query
summary: Jev selects an offered query; delegated preparation and system validation produce executable inputs.

steps.label: Choose the offered query
steps.human:
Consider each query’s purpose, supported questions, required and optional inputs, output fields, source scope, completeness meaning and known limits.

A query is self-describing: for example, an AC-family query accepts a family ID plus population rule and returns attributable AC rows, work status and coverage limits. A title alone is not enough.

Illustrative input contract: family_id (required canonical ID), inclusion (root-excluded or terminal leaves), levels (optional). Output contract: AC records with canonical_id, work_status, source locator/revision; complete flag, known_count, exact_total only when complete, and limitations. These are conceptual catalog semantics, not a new wire schema. Choose the offered query ID/version and its contract, or a bounded none/clarify outcome. Only a selected query continues to input preparation.
produces: Selected query ID/version and contract, or none/clarify outcome
consumes: Offered query input/output contracts and selected method plan

steps.label: Decide preparation needs
steps.human: Choose trusted-input bypass, generative preparation, bounded fact discovery or clarification. Do not author arguments or invent IDs.

steps.label: Bind known values or dispatch preparation
steps.human: Copy trusted known values, or construct a typed host request with question, query/version, contract and approved context. Persist the matching wait. Retrieval-specific preparation binding is proposed; existing host transport is reused. Terms-only help does not execute the full search child; choosing full search transfers ownership directly to shared attempt comparison.
produces: Known arguments or typed host request

steps.label: Optionally propose arguments
steps.human: Propose schema-bound arguments with their basis or unresolved inputs. Never invent canonical IDs/source facts. Skip when known inputs suffice.

steps.label: Validate arguments and resume
steps.human: Validate interaction/state/actor/schema, query/version/source, scope, required fields and budget. Reject unresolved or invalid inputs; prevent duplicate execution. Missing facts route to discovery or clarification.

steps.label: Judge argument adequacy
steps.human: Choose execute, correction, discovery, clarification or stop against the original need. Structural validity alone is insufficient. Only execute reaches the next execution step; other choices return to their preparation/wait/terminal route.
produces: Execute, correction, discovery, clarification or stop decision

steps.label: Execute and return evidence
steps.human:
Run the selected registered query within trusted scope and budget. Keep canonical sources, exact field meanings and completeness limits with the results.

Schema, permission, version and budget checks remain decisive implementation checks; Jev cannot waive them.

Return these results to [Jev shared attempt comparison](docs/product-truth/flows/leafcutter/retrieve-project-knowledge.flow.json#compare), for every executed query, not only a newly built one. Nonaccepted inputs never reach this step.

Return this attempt and its limits to [shared attempt comparison](docs/product-truth/flows/leafcutter/retrieve-project-knowledge.flow.json#compare) alongside prior or complementary methods. The main route owns comparison, advisory recording and combination once.
consumes: Valid scoped arguments with an explicit Jev execute decision

branches.label: No suitable registered query
branches.condition: No catalog output contract can answer the need although required data is supported
branches.human: Enter governed query build; missing data, denied scope or outage remain explicit non-build outcomes. Select another permitted method at [method selection](docs/product-truth/flows/leafcutter/retrieve-project-knowledge.flow.json#plan) when it can help. Build remains eligible only for a proven query gap, not missing data.

provenance.note:
Target design — not a delivery claim
User-requested question-first design. This flow is spec/draft; existing runtime and test evidence do not establish this full contract. Existing acceptance criteria are context pending behavioral mapping, not new completion proof.

Traversal and multiple-method design extension
Added bounded method selection/return routes and a shared attempt-comparison handoff. Target specification only; no runtime or acceptance-status change.
